extracted.intended_audience: short-story writers / fiction writers seeking craft guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Practical craft guidance for composing short stories that are concept-driven, economical, and character-focused; emphasizes tight plotting, showing through action and dialogue, and minimal description. Aimed at writers producing short-form fiction (stories whose timeframe is often days to weeks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider Your Plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep storyline straightforward and concept-driven. "Stories are more about concepts...and driven by characters, so you want to keep it straightforward on the plot level, deep on the concept level." Timeframe of days to weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer a simple, clear plot that serves a strong central concept; avoid sprawling or overly complex plotting in short fiction. Aim for a short story timeframe (days to weeks) so the plot remains focused and manageable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put Action Over Exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Show character development through actions rather than telling. Character traits should emerge from what characters do; actions propel the narrative more than exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scenes and character behavior to reveal inner life and change; minimize authorial summarizing or explanatory exposition that tells rather than shows. Let choices and actions create momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep Dialogue Precise
rubrics_metrics.description: Make dialogue economical and telling; have characters respond obliquely or reveal personality through answers. Example: answering "How are you?" with an unexpected response that hints at the situation creates intrigue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim small-talk and filler; each line of dialogue should either advance plot, reveal character, or create subtext. Use surprising or indirect replies to suggest backstory or tension without explicit explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Spare with Description
rubrics_metrics.description: Select one or two telling details rather than elaborate descriptions. A single distinctive feature lets readers fill in the rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid long, exhaustive descriptions; choose a few vivid, specific details that stand in for a fuller picture. Trust readers' imagination to supply what you omit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize Characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate personality through behavior and speech. "You can tell the reader that a character is nasty, or better yet, you can make them behave or speak in a nasty way."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor showing character through actions, choices, and voice over telling. Use dialogue, gestures, and small behaviors to convey who a character is and how they change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy in All Aspects (Key Principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Louise Marburg: "economy in all aspects is the key" to successful short story writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply economy to plot, prose, dialogue, description, and characterization: be concise, eliminate what doesn't serve the core concept, and let implication and brevity strengthen the story's impact.
